# Event modeling syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-eventmodeling/grammar/eventmodeling.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Event modeling syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `eventmodeling` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed event models with Langium (`event-modeling.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; on a line with `style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` /
`#123;` entities read as opaque text; and a line break appended. Unlike most diagrams, `%%`
comment lines stay in the text (the lexer skips them) and leading blanks are not trimmed.
Keywords are case-sensitive.

Whitespace, line breaks included, separates tokens and nothing more: statements need no line
of their own, and `eventmodeling tf 01 evt A tf 02 evt B` is two frames. A keyword is a keyword
only as a whole word (`tf01` and `evtA` are names), and no name can be a keyword. `title`,
`accTitle` and `accDescr` are read only after a blank on the line of an earlier token (`eventmodeling
title My model`); at the start of a line they are names, which no statement takes.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

An event model is `eventmodeling`, then statements. The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and comment
tokens of the lexer are skipped before parsing.

```ebnf
eventmodeling = Header { statement } EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = HEADER ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Frame
          | Entity
          | Data
          | Note
          | Gwt
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr ;
```

A frame's kind, which picks its lane.

```ebnf
kind = UI
     | PCR
     | PROCESSOR
     | CMD
     | COMMAND
     | RMO
     | READMODEL
     | EVT
     | EVENT ;
```

`` `json` `` (…): how the data is written; not used in drawing.

```ebnf
dataType = BACKTICK ( JSON | JSOBJ | FIGMA | SALT | URI | MD | HTML | TEXT ) BACKTICK ;
```

`Name` or `Namespace.Name`: a two-part name puts the frame in its namespace's lane.

```ebnf
qualifiedName = ID { DOT ID } ;
```

`tf 01 evt Name`, then its sources (`->> 01`), a `[[data]]` reference and inline data, in
that order, each optional.

```ebnf
Frame @Frame = ( TF | TIMEFRAME | RF | RESETFRAME ) FRAME_ID kind qualifiedName { Source } [ OPEN_REF ID CLOSE_REF ] [ [ dataType ] DATA_INLINE ] ;
```

```ebnf
Source @Source = ARROW FRAME_ID ;
```

```ebnf
Entity @Entity = ENTITY qualifiedName ;
```

```ebnf
Data @Data = DATA ID [ dataType ] DATA_BLOCK ;
```

```ebnf
Note @Note = NOTE FRAME_ID [ dataType ] DATA_BLOCK ;
```

`gwt 01 given <kind> <Name> … [when …] then …`: each part lists one or more steps.

```ebnf
Gwt @Gwt = GWT FRAME_ID GIVEN step { step } [ WHEN step { step } ] THEN step { step } ;
```

```ebnf
step = kind ID ;
```

`title …`: the title, after another token on its line (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | HEADER | `eventmodeling(?=\s\|%%\|$)` |  | `eventmodeling`: starts an event model. It ends at a blank, a line break, `%%` or the end of the text. |
| INITIAL | RESETFRAME | `resetframe(?!\w)` |  | `resetframe 01 evt Name`: a frame that starts a new flow: no relation is drawn to it unless it names its sources with `->>`. |
| INITIAL | READMODEL | `readmodel(?!\w)` |  | `readmodel`: a read model frame, in the Command/Read Model lane (as `rmo`). |
| INITIAL | PROCESSOR | `processor(?!\w)` |  | `processor`: an automated processor frame, in the UI/Automation lane (as `pcr`). |
| INITIAL | TIMEFRAME | `timeframe(?!\w)` |  | `timeframe 01 evt Name`: a frame, the next step on the time line (as `tf`). |
| INITIAL | COMMAND | `command(?!\w)` |  | `command`: a command frame, in the Command/Read Model lane (as `cmd`). |
| INITIAL | ENTITY | `entity(?!\w)` |  | `entity Name`: declares an entity, which `gwt` steps name. It is not drawn. |
| INITIAL | EVENT | `event(?!\w)` |  | `event`: an event frame, in the Events lane (as `evt`). |
| INITIAL | JSOBJ | `jsobj(?!\w)` |  | `` `jsobj` ``: data written as a JavaScript object (the type is not used in drawing). |
| INITIAL | FIGMA | `figma(?!\w)` |  | `` `figma` ``: data that is a Figma reference (the type is not used in drawing). |
| INITIAL | GIVEN | `given(?!\w)` |  | `given`: the steps a `gwt` starts from. |
| INITIAL | JSON | `json(?!\w)` |  | `` `json` ``: data written as JSON (the type is not used in drawing). |
| INITIAL | SALT | `salt(?!\w)` |  | `` `salt` ``: data written as a PlantUML Salt wireframe (the type is not used in drawing). |
| INITIAL | HTML | `html(?!\w)` |  | `` `html` ``: data written as HTML (the type is not used in drawing; it shows as text). |
| INITIAL | TEXT | `text(?!\w)` |  | `` `text` ``: data that is plain text. |
| INITIAL | DATA | `data(?!\w)` |  | `data Name { … }`: a named data block, which frames show with `[[Name]]`. |
| INITIAL | NOTE | `note(?!\w)` |  | `note 01 { … }`: a note on a frame. It is not drawn. |
| INITIAL | WHEN | `when(?!\w)` |  | `when`: the steps of a `gwt` that act. |
| INITIAL | THEN | `then(?!\w)` |  | `then`: the steps a `gwt` expects. |
| INITIAL | RMO | `rmo(?!\w)` |  | `rmo`: a read model frame, in the Command/Read Model lane. |
| INITIAL | CMD | `cmd(?!\w)` |  | `cmd`: a command frame, in the Command/Read Model lane. |
| INITIAL | EVT | `evt(?!\w)` |  | `evt`: an event frame, in the Events lane. |
| INITIAL | PCR | `pcr(?!\w)` |  | `pcr`: an automated processor frame, in the UI/Automation lane. |
| INITIAL | URI | `uri(?!\w)` |  | `` `uri` ``: data that is a link (the type is not used in drawing). |
| INITIAL | ARROW | `->>` |  | `->> 01`: the frame this one takes its input from; a frame may name several. Without one, the frame is joined to the nearest earlier frame in another lane. |
| INITIAL | GWT | `gwt(?!\w)` |  | `gwt 01 given … when … then …`: a given/when/then specification of a frame. It is not drawn. |
| INITIAL | UI | `ui(?!\w)` |  | `ui`: a user interface frame, in the UI/Automation lane. |
| INITIAL | MD | `md(?!\w)` |  | `` `md` ``: data written as Markdown (the type is not used in drawing). |
| INITIAL | TF | `tf(?!\w)` |  | `tf 01 evt Name`: a frame, the next step on the time line: an id of one to three digits, a kind, a name, then optionally its sources, a `[[data]]` reference and inline data. |
| INITIAL | OPEN_REF | `\[\[` |  | `[[Name]]`: shows the data block `Name` in the frame. |
| INITIAL | CLOSE_REF | `\]\]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RF | `rf(?!\w)` |  | `rf 01 evt Name`: a reset frame (as `resetframe`). |
| INITIAL | BACKTICK | ``` |  | The backticks around a data type: `` `json` ``. |
| INITIAL | DOT | `\.` |  | `.` in a qualified name: `Inventory.ItemAdded` puts the frame in the lane of its namespace. |
| INITIAL | ID | `[_a-zA-Z][\w_]*` |  | A name: ASCII letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`. |
| INITIAL | FRAME_ID | `\d{1,3}` |  | A frame id: one to three digits (`0`, `00` and `01` are three ids). |
| INITIAL | DATA_INLINE | `\{(.*)\}\|"(.*)"\|'(.*)'` |  | Inline data: `{` to the last `}` on its line, or `"…"` or `'…'` to the last quote of its kind on the line. |
| INITIAL | DATA_BLOCK | `\{[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?\}(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A data block: `{` at the end of its line, the lines of data, then `}` on a line of its own. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr(?:[\t ]*:([^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)\|\s*\{([^}]*)\})` |  | `accDescr: …` to `%%` or the line end, or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description, after another token on its line. |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …` to `%%` or the line end: the accessible title, after another token on its line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …` to `%%` or the line end: the title (not drawn), after another token on its line. |
| INITIAL | — | `\s+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line: a comment. |
| INITIAL | BLOCK_COMMENT | `\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/` |  | `/* … */`: a comment, over lines. |
| INITIAL | LINE_COMMENT | `\/\/[^\n\r]*` |  | `//` to the end of the line: a comment. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
